purpose: Pimecrolimus is used to treat mild to moderate eczema (atopic dermatitis), especially on sensitive areas like the face and skin folds. It helps relieve itching, redness, and irritation caused by eczema. It is often used when other treatments like mild steroid creams have not worked or are not suitable.
how_it_works: Your immune system sometimes overreacts and causes the skin to become inflamed, itchy, and red — that is eczema. Pimecrolimus works by calming down certain immune cells in the skin so they stop triggering that inflammation. Think of it like a 'volume control' that turns down the skin's overactive alarm system without using steroids.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a mild burning, stinging, or warmth at the spot where you apply it, especially in the first few days of use. This usually gets better as your skin adjusts. Some people may also notice temporary redness or itching right after applying it.
warnings: Do not use this cream on infected skin — treat any skin infection first. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen, as this medication may increase sun sensitivity. There is a rare, theoretical concern about a possible link to certain cancers (like lymphoma), so do not use it continuously for long periods without talking to your doctor. Keep it away from eyes and mucous membranes. Not recommended for children under 2 years old.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin layer to the affected skin area twice a day (morning and evening). Gently rub it in until it disappears. Wash your hands after applying unless your hands are the area being treated. Use it only on the areas of skin your doctor has told you to treat, and only for as long as needed.
